Asha L.: Quick flag — I noticed p95 drift on routes labeled `text-long` after yesterday's kernel-fallback patch. Up ~30ms on canary nodes.
Miguel R.: huh. saw that too in the dashboards, thanks. Any strong correlation with KV hit rate or microbatch size?
Asha L.: preliminary correlation with KV miss spikes. When miss% > 12% we see more kernel fallbacks and a longer tail.
Priya K.: do you have a perf trace? can you paste the hot stacks or flamegraph link?
Asha L.: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood.internal/flame/1746789012-p95. Quick excerpt attached.
Asha L.: ```
# top samples
runtime::serve_loop 32%
kernel_switcher::select 18%
kv_cache::fetch_miss 15%
decoder::attn_kernel_fallback 12%
``` 
Miguel R.: interesting — a fair chunk is in the kernel switch + decoder fallback. That explains token-level latency hits.
Priya K.: so batch formation interacts with cache behavior. If a request arrives and prefixed KV miss, we spin up fallback kernel => higher per-token cost => queue backpressure.
Asha L.: my read: our token budget allocator currently assumes stable kernel cost per token. With fallback the cost spikes and the token budget per route is too generous.
Miguel R.: proposes: make token budget dynamic per-route using recent KV hit rate and measured kernel time. call it "traffic warden" heuristic.
Priya K.: love the name :smile: Can you sketch the formula? we need something simple for rollout.
Miguel R.: sketch: budget_target(route) = base_tokens * min(1.0, (kv_hit_rate * alpha) + (1 - kernel_slowdown) * beta). alpha/beta tuned so hit_rate dominates.
Miguel R.: Practically: if kv_hit_rate drops to 50% and kernel slowdown factor > 1.3, budget scales down to ~60% of base.
Asha L.: also add a short-term EWMA (30s) and a longer-term EWMA (5m) to avoid oscillation.
Priya K.: agree. also want a safety floor per tier so SLOs for high-tier customers aren't starved. floor: 30% of base for platinum.
Miguel R.: canary plan: enable traffic-warden on route-group `text-long` in canary cluster A, with kernel_fallback tracing enabled, and reduced budget by 25% initially.
Asha L.: I'll run microbenchmarks to calibrate alpha/beta. Quick script I used:
Asha L.: ```
# simulate
for hit in [0.9,0.7,0.5,0.3]:
  slow = 1 + (0.4*(1-hit))
  budget = 512 * min(1.0, (hit*0.8) + (1 - (slow-1))*0.2)
  print(hit, slow, budget)
``` 
PerfBot: PerfBot noticed metric bump: canary-A kv_miss_rate 14% at 12:02 UTC, p95 increased by 32ms.
Priya K.: action items: 1) Asha run perf microbench and post numbers 2) Miguel implement traffic-warden toggle + telemetry 3) ramp plan in ops runbook
Asha L.: I'll post microbench results in ~2 hours. starting with 4 kernel variants and kv miss sim.
Miguel R.: I'll add `traffic_warden.enabled` flag + `route_kv_hit` and `route_kernel_cost` metrics to the stats pipeline.
Priya K.: Ops: avoid global rollout. canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with regress guard: p95 <= baseline + 10ms and error rate unchanged.
Asha L.: noted. also will add a small experiment to reduce microbatch max_tokens from 512 to 384 to see interaction.
Miguel R.: if we see regressions, fallback plan is auto-disable and revert to previous budgeter.
Priya K.: perfect. keep discussion here. please tag me when you have numbers. :thumbsup:
